Gold Bust

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After our expose' on the illicit gold trade in September this year we join a massive police raid on illegal gold traders in Welkom

Summary:
Following our expose' on the illegal gold trade the Hawks promised swift action against people involved. Carte Blanche was given exclusive access to a massive police operation taking place in Welkom in the Free State, an illegal gold hotspot.

Further information:
Operation Grandiose is the culmination of a two year undercover sting operation by a joint police task force involving members from Crime Intelligence, DPCI and SAPS. As part of the operation, police went undercover and participated in a variety of illegal gold deals to identify various smugglers, dealers and kingpins in the industry. They managed to obtain warrants of arrest for 63 suspects. The arrests were executed on tuesday night this week, in a massive secret operation involving more than 500 police members. Police were split into groups of about ten members and the arrests took place simultaneously. We were allowed to join one of these groups as they raided suspects in the Thabong Township next to Welkom. Our group managed to arrest two of the four suspects on their list. By 6am on tuesday morning we joined polce at their Joint Operations Center and they had managed to arrest about half of the 63 suspects. The operation is scheduled to last for three days and police will confirm how many arrests were made by the end of the op.

Viewing / Editorial input


Viewing Notes:
13/11/2014 03:06:37 PM
AMALIA NOTES
Explain where all the cops were from – which provinces
Explain that they met at the Pakhisa Race Way
Needs more drama
Needs to show us what you are saying – when you talk about the gun holster doesn’t match the gun holster we are seeing.
Flesh out the original story more – you refer in one line to the VAT SCAM but someone who hasn’t seen it wont understand it – leave the VAT SCAM out and focus on the Zama Zamas - the audience needs to understand why the police is going so far – why so many cops on one operation.
You will need to blur the faces of the suspects
Show more of the Zama Zamas going down the holes we have told those stories
Now we are at welkom – get something that says you are in Welkom a mining town and that is why the hawks have descended on Welkom – where ? Phakisa
Restate the context clearly and broadly
We also need to see more of the result of it – have they hit a syndicate what have they done

Start with the action - it with the raid and all those 500 police in Welkom and then work backwards – this is why they are here. Treat this like a news story... why are they doing this? because its NB because this is what has been going on...
You can end with ramaloko

Stings don’t work they are not stories they are elements of a story.

Press Release:


Hawks Gold Raid
This week saw the culmination of a two-year undercover sting by a joint police task force boldly named Operation Grandiose. Carte Blanche’s cameras captured exclusive footage of a night raid by over 500 law enforcement officers into the Thabong Township near Welkom to arrest multiple illegal gold syndicate suspects.


Script:


Gold Bust
12 Nov 2014
1st Draft Script

Visuals: Breaking open the lock

V/O:
Tuesday this week, and a 2am wake-up call for members of the illegal gold trade as hundreds of police descended on the small Free State mining town of Welkom.

Sound-Up:
Vula-vula-vula

V/O:
The police have 63 suspects in their sights, most of them are mid-level or major players in the underground world of illicit gold.

Voice:
Illegal gold mining is rife in South Africa. Carte Blanche has brought you numerous stories showing the lengths that zamazamas will go to to get their hands on just a little bit of gold. It’s a violent and dangerous trade.

Sound Up Chris Zulu
Because there is a lot of fighting in this illegal mining – shooting, killing each other.

Voice:
It’s a lucrative industry, estimates are that 10 percent of all gold that’s mined in South Africa is stolen and makes its way onto the black market. Along with smuggled gold and gold from illegal mining operations, this is an industry worth billions. Because of the money involved, the Hawks have designated it a priority crime.

Link Susan
Two years ago the Hawks launched Operation Grandiose in Welkom in the Free State. There are literally hundreds of members of the police and the Hawks gathered here. It’s just after midnight and they’re about to launch a massive operation – and they’ve given Carte Blanche exclusive access.

Voice
Over 500 law enforcement officials from 4 different provinces gathered in secret at the Phakisa Raceway just outside of town. Present were members of the Hawks, the Organized Crime Unit and Crime Intelligence, who were split into 40 different teams that would launch simultaneous raids across town.


Sound Up Policeman:
The agent already told you more or less what you will find at what address, so go and look for those items.

Voice
Secrecy was crucial. To ensure the suspects weren’t tipped off, their names and whereabouts were only revealed to the police just minutes before the operation commenced.

Voice
As it started pouring with rain, our convoy headed to a well-known mining hostel in the Thabong Township.

Link Susan
It’s now two am and we’re at G Hostel, one of the main targets of the operation. Police are about to move in and they’re hoping to catch their suspects at home and asleep.

Voice
While armed policemen covered the multitude of alleyways and blind corners, members of the tactical response unit started waking up their suspects.

Sound Up Police buzz (warrant of arrest)

Voice
Two years worth of undercover work was finally paying off – the police already had all the evidence they needed against their suspects and warrants of arrest had already been issued. It was now just a case of bringing them in, and searching the houses for weapons, cash and any tools of the illegal mining trade.

Sound Up Police buzz

Voice
But the police were also on the hunt for cellphones and laptops.

Sound up
(police woman from earlier, we need their pins)

Voice
On hand were several high-tech Digital Forensic Labs to download contacts, SMSes and pictures which could provide crucial intelligence going forward.

Voice
By 6am the next morning 30 of the 63 suspects were in custody at Joint Operational Command, a temporary base outside of town.

Sound Up Paul Ramaloko
It has been a fruitful six hours, where half of our targets are now behind bars…

Voice:
Captain Paul Ramaloko from the Hawks says they’re confident that these arrests will send shockwaves through the entire illegal trade.

Sound Up Paul Ramaloko
They will be facing charges in contravention of the organized crime act and all their charges will be taken from that angle.
